theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is the main aim of monitoring quality during production welding, and not only at final inspection?
options: To give the final inspector less paperwork to fill in at the end
To catch a drift early, before many parts are spoiled
To let the welders work without any written procedure at all
To make sure every part is inspected twice by two people

questions.stem: On a run of 200 welded brackets, what is a "first-off" inspection?
options: A check of the part the welder likes best from the batch
A check of every tenth part once the whole run is finished
A check of the jig only, with no part fitted in it at all
A full check of the first part before the run goes on

questions.stem: Why is the last part of a production run also checked and kept for a time?
options: It shows the process was still right at the end
It is the best-looking part, so it is kept for show
It is given to the welder as a reward for the run
It is used to set up a different job the next day

questions.stem: What is patrol (in-process) inspection on a welding line?
options: A security guard's walk round the yard at night
An inspection done only when a customer complains
Checks made at set times at each work station
A check made once a year by an outside auditor

questions.stem: On a GMAW production line, why are the wire speed, voltage and gas flow checked and logged at set times during the shift?
options: So the electricity used by each set can be charged to the job
Settings can drift, and the log shows they stayed in range
So the welders can be paid by the amount of wire they use
So the gas supplier knows when to deliver the next cylinder

questions.stem: Some welding sets can record the current and voltage of every weld. How does this help to monitor quality?
options: Welds made outside the limits can be found and checked
It lets the set weld by itself without a welder present
It means no other inspection of the welds is ever needed
It stops the welder from changing any setting on the set

questions.stem: A run chart plots the fillet leg size of every tenth bracket. The last seven points are all above the centre line, but inside the limits. What does this suggest?
options: All is well, as every point is inside the limits
The gauge must be broken, so it should be thrown away
The welder should be moved to another job at once
The process has shifted and should be looked at

questions.stem: A point on a control chart falls outside a control limit. What should happen?
options: Leave it off the chart, as it spoils the pattern
Move the limit out so that the point fits inside
Stop, find the cause and check the parts just made
Wait for two more points outside before acting

questions.stem: What is the difference between a control limit and a tolerance (specification) limit?
options: They are the same thing, simply written in two different ways on the chart
Control limits show the normal spread; tolerance is what the drawing allows
Control limits are set by the customer, while the tolerance is set by the welder
Control limits are for welds only; tolerance is for the paint only

questions.stem: A shift welded 120 m of fillet weld and found 6 defects. How many defects is that per 10 m of weld?
Of 250 welded frames, 230 passed inspection first time. What is the first-time pass rate?
The weld repair rate over five weeks reads 2%, 2.5%, 3.5%, 4.5% and 6%. What should the quality monitor do?
options: Wait until it passes 10%, as it is still low for now
Nothing, as every week is still under the old limit
Report it at the end of the year in the yearly review
Raise it now, as there is a clear rising trend

questions.stem: A crack is found in a production weld. Before looking for the cause, what is the first step?
options: Hold and check the parts made since the last good check
Find out which welder made it and send him home
Repair the crack quietly and carry on with the run
Write a new WPS for the joint before anything else

questions.stem: After a failure in a sample, the inspection plan says to "tighten" the sampling. What does this mean?
options: Check fewer parts so the line can catch up on output
Check more parts until the results are good again
Tighten every bolt on the parts in the sample
Ask the customer to check the parts for the shop

questions.stem: Why is a board of photos showing acceptable and rejectable welds put up at a production station?
options: To decorate the station and make it look modern
To show visitors which welders are the best ones
So welders and inspectors judge welds the same way
So the photos can be used in the sales brochure

questions.stem: Why is a short, illustrated work instruction posted at each production welding station?
options: So the welders do not need any training at all
So the inspector has less to check at final inspection
So the customer can see it when they visit the shop
So each welder works the same approved way each time

questions.stem: Why are the jigs and fixtures on a production line checked at set intervals?
options: Worn or moved stops make every part wrong
Jigs must be repainted every month for safety
The jigs are counted to stop them being stolen
So the jigs can be used for a different job

questions.stem: A jig is made so a bracket can only be fitted into it the right way round. What is this an example of?
options: Statistical sampling
Final inspection
Mistake-proofing
Quality auditing

questions.stem: A batch of welding wire is found to be faulty. How do the production records help?
options: They show the price paid for the faulty wire batch
They show which parts were welded with that batch
They show which welder ordered the faulty batch
They show how many spools are left in the store

questions.stem: Two inspectors measure the same fillet weld and record 6 mm and 8 mm. What should the quality monitor do first?
options: Take the average, 7 mm, and record that as the result
Accept the larger reading, as it favours the welder
Ask the welder which of the two readings is right
Check the gauges and how each inspector measures

questions.stem: What does a process audit of a production welding line mainly check?
options: That every finished part is the right size
That the welders are paid on time each week
That the line works to its procedures and records
That the building is insured against fire

questions.stem: Which of these is a cost of poor quality on a welding line?
options: Grinding out and rewelding rejected joints
Training welders before a new job begins
Buying a fillet gauge for each work station
Writing a work instruction for each station

questions.stem: Rework took 18 hours last month at J$2 500 an hour, plus J$15 000 of consumables. What did the rework cost in total?
Who should be allowed to stop a production welding line for a serious quality problem?
options: Only the owner of the company, and no one else
Only the customer, when he visits the workshop
Only the inspector, after the shift has finished
Anyone who finds the fault, as the system allows

questions.stem: What quality information should be passed on at a shift change on a welding line?
options: The number of tea breaks taken on the shift
Who arrived late and who left early that day
Open problems, parts on hold and setting changes
The music the welders want played in the bay

questions.stem: Frames coming off the line are slowly going out of square during the week. Which check is most likely to find the cause?
options: Check the jig, the tack order and the weld sequence
Check the colour of the primer used on the frames
Check how many frames the customer has ordered
Check the weather forecast for the coming week

questions.stem: The production manager wants to switch to a cheaper welding wire. What should happen before the change?
options: Switch at once, as all wire of the same size is alike
Check the WPS covers it, trial it and approve it in writing
Switch, and wait to see if the customer complains
Use the new wire only on the night shift at first

questions.stem: Why is defect data recorded against each welder number and machine, as well as each defect type?
options: So the welders can be ranked on a board for a prize
So the store can charge each welder for the wire used
So the machines can be sold off in order of age
It shows if a fault comes from a person, method or machine

questions.stem: Porosity has risen only on the night shift. What is the best next step?
options: Compare night conditions, settings and staff with the day
Stop the night shift and move all work to the day
Tell the night welders to take more care from now on
Ask the day shift to repair the night shift's welds

questions.stem: Last month's faults were: porosity 40, undercut 25, spatter 15, wrong size 10, other 10. What share of all faults is porosity?
Why should production quality results be shown on a board at the line, where the welders can see them?
options: So the welders' families can see them on visiting day
So welders see the results and help fix problems sooner
So the inspector can take the rest of the week off
So the customer can choose which welder does his job

questions.stem: Why is 100% final inspection alone a poor way to control quality on a busy production line?
options: It is too cheap, so managers do not value it
It makes every part pass, whatever its faults
It is only allowed on parts for overseas clients
It finds faults late, and some are still missed

questions.stem: Patrol checks show that fillet welds are often 2 mm larger than the drawing asks. Why is this a quality problem?
options: Larger welds are always weaker than smaller ones
Oversize welds cannot be measured with a gauge
It wastes wire and time and adds distortion
The paint will not cover a larger fillet weld

questions.stem: A production WPS calls for preheat on thick base plates. How should the monitor check that it is done on every part?
options: Spot checks with crayons, and a sign-off on each part's record
Ask the welders at the end of the week if they remembered
Feel each plate with a bare hand before welding starts
Assume it is done, as the WPS is posted at the station

questions.stem: Repaired welds are going to the paint shop without being inspected again. What should the monitor do?
options: Let it go on, as repairs are made by the best welders
Stop it: repairs must pass the same checks again
Ask the painter to look at the repairs as he paints
Inspect only one repair in every ten from now on

questions.stem: Welded parts are going to be hot-dip galvanised with spatter and slag still on them. Why is this a quality problem?
options: The zinc will make the spatter grow larger in the bath
Spatter makes the parts too heavy for the galvanising crane
Slag and spatter spoil the coating and its finish
The galvaniser will charge more for parts with spatter

questions.stem: A process makes fillet legs between 6.2 mm and 7.8 mm. The drawing allows 6 mm to 8 mm. What does this tell the monitor?
options: The process is perfect and needs no more checks
The drawing should be changed to 6.2 to 7.8 mm
Every part must now be measured three times
It only just fits, so any drift will cause rejects

questions.stem: On a production control plan, what is a reaction plan?
options: What to do when a check fails, written in advance
A plan for the staff party at the end of the job
The order in which the parts are delivered to site
A list of welders who react fastest in an emergency

questions.stem: The plan says to check 1 part in every 20. A shift makes 340 parts. How many parts are checked?
A patrol check sheet has been filled in for a time when nobody was working on the line. What should happen?
options: Nothing, as the sheet looks complete and tidy
Tear out the page and fill it in again neatly
Report it, as the record is false and the checks unknown
Ask the night watchman to sign it as a witness

questions.stem: A new welder joins the line. Before he welds production parts, what should the monitor confirm?
options: That he can work longer hours than the other welders
That he has brought his own welding set and helmet
That he has worked for a big company in Kingston before
He is qualified and has passed a trial piece on the line

questions.stem: A customer's order asks for 100% visual inspection and 5% magnetic particle testing on all production welds. Where should this be written?
options: On the control plan and the job's inspection records
Only in the sales file, as it is part of the price
On the delivery note, after the parts are sent
Nowhere, as the inspector will remember it

questions.stem: What should a monthly quality report for a production welding line include?
options: The welders' holiday dates and their phone numbers
Only the total number of parts made in the month
Trends, the main faults, costs, and the actions taken
A copy of every inspection sheet from the whole month

questions.stem: Why do weld defects found at the customer's site cost far more than the same defects found on the line?
options: Site welders are always paid twice the shop rate
Travel, removal and site rework add a lot of cost
Defects found on site are always much larger
The customer pays nothing for defects found on site

questions.stem: After a change to the tack order, distortion rejects fall from 8% to 2% and stay there for six weeks. What should be done?
options: Go back to the old order, as the test is over now
Keep the change secret so other lines do not copy it
Stop checking for distortion, as the problem is solved
Make the new order standard in the work instruction

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What two-word name is given to the full check of the first part made on a production run, before the rest go ahead?
On an 8-hour shift, a patrol check is made every 30 minutes. How many patrol checks are made in the shift?
What is the name of the chart that plots a measurement in time order, with a centre line and upper and lower limits worked out from the process?
What Japanese term is used for designing a jig or method so that a mistake cannot be made?
In quality cost terms, what two-word name is given to the cost of a fault found by the customer after delivery?
What is the name of a marked sample weld kept at the station to show the worst appearance that may still be accepted?
What name is given to an audit that checks finished parts against the drawing, as opposed to a process audit?
Which group of quality costs covers training welders and designing good jigs to stop faults happening?
What is the name of the first step after a fault is found, in which suspect parts are held and checked so that no more bad parts move on?
Quality costs are often split into prevention, appraisal and failure costs. In which of these groups does inspection belong?
What is the name of the bar chart that ranks fault types from the most common to the least common?
What is the name of the document that lists, for each production step, the check to make, how often, the method and what to do if it fails?
A shift welded 150 brackets and 6 were rejected. What percentage were rejected?
What is the name of the part made at the start of a shift to prove the set-up, which is then cut up or tested and not sent out?
What is the name of the device fitted to some welding sets that records the current and voltage of each weld for later checking?

essays.stem: Your shop is to make 500 welded window grille frames for a housing scheme in St Catherine. Explain how you would set up quality monitoring for the production run.
essays.modelAnswer: I would start with the drawing, the specification and the customer's inspection needs, and write a control plan. For each step (cutting, fitting in the jig, tacking, welding, cleaning and finishing) it would list the check, the method, how often, who does it and the reaction plan if a check fails. Before the run, the jig is checked against the drawing, the WPS settings are set, and a first-off frame is fully inspected and signed before production starts. During the run, patrol checks at set times cover dimensions, diagonals, weld size and appearance against a photo board, and the settings are logged. The sample rate is tightened if a failure is found. Each batch is marked so its welder, wire batch and checks can be traced. Results go on a run chart and a board at the line. The last-off frame is checked and kept. Faults are contained, recorded and acted on, and a weekly summary goes to management.
markingPoints: Control plan from the drawing, specification and customer needs, with reaction plans
Set-up checks and a signed first-off inspection
Patrol checks at set times, settings logged, sampling tightened on failure
Traceability by batch; results charted and shown at the line
Last-off check; faults contained and acted on; regular reporting

essays.stem: Explain how first-off, patrol and last-off checks work together to control the quality of a production run, and what each one proves.
essays.modelAnswer: The first-off check is a full inspection of the first part made after a set-up. It proves that the jig, the settings, the materials and the method can make a good part, before many parts are made. If it fails, the set-up is corrected and another first-off is made. Patrol checks are made at set times or intervals during the run, on sample parts and on the settings. They prove that the process is staying in control, and catch drift from wear, heat, tiredness or a new batch of materials while only a few parts are affected. The last-off check is made on the final part of the run. It proves that the process was still good at the end, so the whole run can be released. If it fails, every part back to the last good patrol check is suspect and must be checked. Together they bracket every part between good checks, and the records show it.
markingPoints: First-off: full check after set-up; proves the set-up; correct and repeat if it fails
Patrol: checks at set times; proves the process stays in control and catches drift
Last-off: proves the process was good at the end; release of the run
Failure means parts back to the last good check are suspect
Together they bracket the run, shown in records

essays.stem: Explain how you would set up and use a run chart or control chart to monitor a welding measurement, such as fillet leg size, on a production line.
essays.modelAnswer: I would choose a measurement that matters, such as fillet leg size, and decide how often to sample it, for example one part in ten. I would mark the target as the centre line and draw the drawing's tolerance limits. For a control chart, after collecting about 20 to 25 readings from a steady process, I would work out the average and the normal spread and draw control limits, which are usually inside the tolerance. Each reading is plotted in time order by the person who measures it. I would act when a point falls outside a control limit, when a run of points sits on one side of the centre line, or when points climb or fall steadily, because each of these shows the process has changed. The action is to stop, check the recent parts, find the cause (settings, jig, consumables, welder) and correct it, then note the cause on the chart. The chart is kept at the line, so the welders can see it.
markingPoints: Chooses a key measurement and a sampling rate
Centre line, tolerance limits, and control limits worked out from steady data
Readings plotted in time order
Signals named: point outside limits, runs on one side, steady trends
Action: stop, check parts, find and fix the cause, note it on the chart, display it

essays.stem: Describe how welding settings and consumables are monitored during production welding, and explain why each check matters.
essays.modelAnswer: The settings on the WPS for each station, such as current or wire speed, voltage, gas flow and travel speed, are checked at the start of each shift and at set times during it. Wire speed can be checked by timing a run-out, current and voltage with a calibrated meter or the set's data logger, and gas flow with a flowmeter at the nozzle. Each reading is written on the station log. These checks matter because settings drift, knobs get moved, and cables and tips wear, and any of these can cause lack of fusion, porosity or wrong weld size on many parts before anyone notices. Consumables are checked when loaded: the wire class and batch, the gas type, and that low-hydrogen electrodes come from the oven. The batch numbers are recorded against the parts made. This matters because the wrong or damp consumable can spoil the weld metal, and the records let any faulty batch be traced to the parts it went into.
markingPoints: Settings checked at shift start and set times, against the WPS
Methods: timed run-out, calibrated meter or data logger, flowmeter
Why: drift, worn parts, moved knobs cause defects on many parts
Consumables checked on loading: class, batch, gas, dry electrodes
Batch numbers recorded for traceability

essays.stem: A patrol check finds that fillet welds on a batch of brackets are 2 mm undersize. Describe what you would do, from containing the problem to proving the fix has worked.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would contain it. I would stop the station, tag the parts on hand, and check every bracket made since the last good patrol check, as well as any already moved on to painting or the store. Undersize parts are kept apart in the quarantine area and recorded on a non-conformance report. Next I would find the cause by looking at the facts: the settings log, the wire speed and travel speed, the welder's method, the gauge, the jig, and whether a new wire batch or a new welder started. Asking why several times helps to reach the real cause, for example a wire feed roll slipping, so the welder sped up. I would then correct it: repair or replace the feed roll, reset the settings, and brief the welder. The undersize brackets are repaired to the procedure and inspected again. Finally, I would prove the fix with tighter sampling for a time, watch the run chart, and update the control plan if needed.
markingPoints: Contain: stop, tag and check parts back to the last good check, including parts moved on
Quarantine and record on an NCR
Find the root cause from the facts (settings, method, gauge, jig, materials)
Correct the cause; repair and re-inspect the parts
Prove the fix: tighter sampling, run chart, update the control plan

essays.stem: Explain the four groups of quality costs in a welding shop, with an example of each, and show with figures why spending on prevention usually pays.
essays.modelAnswer: Prevention costs are spent to stop faults happening, such as training welders, writing work instructions, and making good jigs. Appraisal costs are spent on checking, such as patrol inspection, gauges and NDT. Internal failure costs come from faults found before delivery, such as grinding out and rewelding, scrap and lost time. External failure costs come from faults found by the customer, such as site repairs, travel, returns, lost goodwill and claims. As an example, if a shop spends J$100 000 a month on rework and J$40 000 on one site repair, and a J$50 000 jig and training programme halves both, it saves J$70 000 a month for a one-off J$50 000, paying for itself in under a month. Faults cost more the later they are found, because more work has been added to the part and site work is dearer. So money spent on prevention and early checks usually saves much more in failure costs.
markingPoints: Prevention cost with an example
Appraisal cost with an example
Internal failure cost with an example
External failure cost with an example
Worked figures showing prevention pays, and that later faults cost more

essays.stem: Explain how you would use production defect data, split by defect type, welder, shift and machine, to find the cause of a quality problem.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would make sure each defect is recorded with its type, the part, the weld number, the welder, the machine, the shift and the date. I would count the defects by type and draw a Pareto chart, to see which one or two types cause most of the problem; I would work on the biggest first. Then I would split that defect by welder, by machine, by shift and by date. If one welder has most of the defects, the cause may be his training or method. If one machine is the common factor, its settings, cables or feed may be at fault. If one shift is worse, I would look at conditions such as lighting, heat, supervision or staffing. If the defects started on a certain date, I would look for a change then, such as a new wire batch or a moved jig. I would then check the likely cause by trial, put in a fix, and watch the data to confirm it worked.
markingPoints: Defects recorded with type, part, welder, machine, shift and date
Pareto chart to pick the biggest problem
Splitting by welder, machine, shift and date, with what each pattern means
Looking for changes at the start date
Trial the cause, fix it and confirm with the data

essays.stem: Explain how jigs, work instructions, visual standards and mistake-proofing help to build quality into production welding, instead of relying on inspection to find faults.
essays.modelAnswer: A well-made jig locates every part in the same place with fixed stops and clamps, so each assembly has the same fit-up and size, and distortion is controlled. It must be checked at set intervals because wear or a knocked stop makes every part wrong. A short work instruction at each station, with photos, shows the approved method, settings, tack order and weld sequence, so every welder works the same way on every shift. Visual standards, such as a photo board and boundary samples, show what an acceptable and a rejectable weld look like, so welders and inspectors judge alike, and welders can check their own work. Mistake-proofing means designing the jig or method so an error cannot happen or is seen at once, for example a pin that lets a bracket fit only the right way, or a counter on the number of welds. Together these prevent faults at the source, so inspection confirms quality instead of sorting out bad parts.
markingPoints: Jigs: same fit-up and size, distortion control, checked at intervals
Work instructions: same approved method and settings on every shift
Visual standards and boundary samples: welders and inspectors judge alike; self-checking
Mistake-proofing with an example
Explains prevention at the source versus sorting by inspection

essays.stem: Explain how you would control a change on a production welding line, such as a new wire, a new jig or a new welder, so that quality is not lost.
essays.modelAnswer: Any change is first written down and reviewed by the people responsible for quality and production. For a new wire, I would check that its class is covered by the WPS, or get the WPS revised or a new procedure qualified, and check its certificate. For a new jig, I would check it against the drawing before use. For a new welder, I would check his qualification covers the work, give him an induction to the work instruction, and have him weld a trial piece that is inspected. After any change, a first-off part is fully inspected before the run goes on, and patrol sampling is tightened for a time. The change is recorded with its date, so any later faults can be linked to it, and the control plan, work instruction or training record is updated. If results get worse, the change is stopped and reviewed. Changes are approved in writing, not made on the spot by one person.
markingPoints: Change written down, reviewed and approved in writing
New wire: WPS cover or requalification, certificate checked
New jig checked against the drawing; new welder qualified, inducted, trial piece
First-off inspection and tightened sampling after the change
Change recorded with date; documents updated; reversed if results worsen

essays.stem: Describe what should go into a monthly production quality report for a welding line, and how you would present it to management and to the welders.
essays.modelAnswer: The report should give the output for the month and the main quality measures: first-time pass rate, repair rate, defects per metre of weld, scrap and customer returns, compared with targets and the last few months, ideally on simple charts. It should show the main defect types on a Pareto chart, and any patterns by station, shift or welder, kept fair and private where it concerns people. It should give the cost of rework, scrap and site repairs. It should list the non-conformances raised, the corrective actions taken and whether they worked, and the actions planned for next month, with owners and dates. For management, I would present a one-page summary with the trends, costs and decisions needed, such as money for a new jig. For the welders, I would use the board at the line and a short meeting, showing the trends and what is being done, thanking them for improvements and asking for their ideas.
markingPoints: Key measures against targets and past months, with charts
Main defect types and patterns, treated fairly
Cost of poor quality
NCRs, corrective actions, results and next actions with owners
Presented differently to management (summary, decisions) and welders (board, meeting, ideas)

practical1.title: Run and monitor a short production batch of welded brackets: first-off, patrol checks, a run chart and last-off
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a bracket drawing, a WPS, a jig and enough parts for a batch of 10–12 identical welded brackets, with a control plan form. As a group, first write a short control plan: the checks at each step, how often, the tools and the reaction plan. Check the jig against the drawing. Make and fully inspect a first-off bracket and have it signed before the batch goes on. Then make the batch, sharing out the roles and changing them every three or four brackets, so every member welds, every member does a patrol check, and every member logs settings: welder; patrol inspector (dimensions, diagonals, leg size and appearance against the photo board); settings monitor (timed wire run-out or current check, gas flow); and recorder (plots leg size on a run chart and keeps the log with the wire batch number). The assessor may change a setting or knock a jig stop part way through: if a check fails, follow the reaction plan. Check and keep the last-off bracket. Photograph each stage and hand in the control plan, logs, run chart and a short summary.
materials: Bracket drawing, WPS, control plan form and acceptance photo board (from the assessor)
Jig and parts for 10–12 identical brackets
GMAW or MMAW set and consumables to the WPS
Fillet gauges, square, tape, steel rule, stopwatch and flowmeter
Station log, run chart paper and tags for held parts
photos: The written control plan and the jig being checked
A patrol check in progress, with the gauge on a weld
The settings being checked (timed run-out or meter)
The run chart and station log part way through the batch
Any held parts tagged, and the last-off bracket with the finished batch
checklist: Helped write a control plan with checks, frequencies and a reaction plan
Checked the jig and took part in the first-off inspection before production
Welded brackets to the WPS in the jig
Carried out a patrol check accurately and recorded it
Checked and logged the settings correctly
Plotted readings on the run chart and spotted any signal
Followed the reaction plan when a check failed, holding and checking suspect parts
safety: Weld in booths or behind screens, with fume extraction
Wear full PPE when welding and when checking near welding
Treat brackets as hot: use tongs and mark hot parts
Keep the jig area clear and tidy, with cables off the floor where possible

practical2.title: Analyse a month's production quality data and present a quality report with corrective actions
practical2.brief: This task is done on paper or on a computer. The assessor gives the group a pack of made-up production data for one month on a welding line: daily output, inspection results by defect type, welder, machine and shift, rework hours, a J$ labour rate and two customer complaints. As a group, share out the work so that each member produces one part and checks another member's part: (1) the first-time pass rate and repair rate for each week, on a run chart; (2) a Pareto chart of defect types; (3) the main defect split by welder, machine and shift, with what the pattern shows; (4) the cost of rework and complaints for the month; (5) a corrective action plan for the biggest problem, with containment, likely root cause, actions, owners, dates and how the result will be checked. Put the parts together as a short monthly quality report, then present it to the assessor, who plays the production manager, with each member speaking to their part. Treat names in the data fairly and keep them within the group. Photograph each part as it is finished.
materials: Production data pack (made up, from the assessor)
Calculators, graph paper or a computer with a spreadsheet
A3 paper or flip chart for the charts
Report template and corrective action form
A phone or camera for the photos
photos: The group sharing out the tasks
The run chart of weekly pass and repair rates
The Pareto chart of defect types
The analysis by welder, machine and shift
The cost calculation and the corrective action plan
checklist: Worked out rates and costs correctly, showing the working
Drew a clear, correctly ordered chart
Read the data correctly and drew a sound conclusion from it
Wrote a corrective action with containment, cause, owners, dates and a check
Checked another member's part and corrected any errors
Presented their part clearly and answered questions
safety: Keep any names in the data within the group, as you would with real quality records
Present findings about people fairly, without blame
Share the workload fairly and take breaks from screens
